Large Page

Retrieval augmented generation grounds model output in verifiable sources by fetching passages before answering (section 1).

Chunking strategy decides how much context each passage carries, and both extremes degrade retrieval quality (section 2).

Embedding models compress text into dense vectors whose distances approximate semantic similarity (section 3).

Hybrid search blends lexical matching with vector similarity so exact identifiers and paraphrase both work (section 4).

Reranking scores a shortlist of candidate passages against the query and is slower but far more accurate (section 5).

Evaluation of retrieval quality uses recall at k and mean reciprocal rank to measure different failure modes (section 6).

Prompt injection remains open because retrieved content is concatenated into the prompt alongside instructions (section 7).

Caching embeddings avoids recomputing vectors for documents that have not changed since the last request (section 8).

Longer context windows are not a substitute for retrieval because attention degrades over very long inputs (section 9).

Observability means logging the query, the retrieved identifiers, and the final answer together for diagnosis (section 10).
